name: AdvancedSettings

states.name: Initial Loading State
states.description: When the page first mounts, it loads debug settings and device info from the Tauri backend. During this time, a loading indicator is shown. Both loadSettings() and loadDeviceInfo() are called on mount.

states.name: Section Header
states.description: The page header displays an 'Advanced' title with a wrench icon and a description explaining the purpose of the debug settings. This uses the shared SectionHeader component.

states.name: Error Display
states.description: When settings fail to load or save, an error banner is displayed with a red X icon and the error message. The error state is set when Tauri IPC calls fail.
states.precondition: A settings load or save operation has failed

states.name: Save Success Feedback
states.description: After successfully saving settings, a green success banner appears for 3 seconds showing 'Settings saved successfully!'. The save button also briefly changes to show a checkmark and 'Saved!' text.
states.precondition: User has clicked Save and the operation succeeded

states.name: Debug Settings Section
states.description: The Debug section is contained within a rounded card with a 'Debug' heading. It holds the image match debug toggle, the top matches count slider, and an informational note about when settings take effect.

states.name: Image Match Debug Mode Toggle

requiredElements.text: Collect and display detailed match information

states.description: A toggle switch labeled 'Enable Image Match Debug Mode' controls whether detailed match information is collected during image recognition. The toggle has a title and a description explaining what it does. Toggling changes local state; changes are not persisted until the user clicks Save.

states.name: Top Matches Count Control
states.description: A range slider with a companion number input allows users to set how many top match candidates are displayed in debug information. The value is clamped between 1 and 10. Both the slider and the number input are synchronized.
states.precondition: No previously saved debug settings exist

states.name: Settings Effect Note
states.description: An informational note below the debug controls explains when settings take effect. This helps users understand they need to run a new image recognition attempt to see changes.

states.name: Save Debug Settings Button
states.description: A save button at the bottom right of the debug section persists all debug settings to the backend. It shows different states: default ('Save Debug Settings' with a gear icon), saving ('Saving...' with spinner), and saved ('Saved!' with checkmark). The button is disabled during save operations.
states.precondition: User has clicked the save button

states.name: Device Information Section
states.description: A separate card section shows system device information useful for debugging and support. It has a 'Device Information' heading with a monitor icon, a refresh button, a description, and three device fields: Device ID, Device Name, and Platform. Each field is clickable to copy its value to the clipboard.

states.name: Device ID Field
states.description: The Device ID field displays the unique device identifier in monospace font. It is a clickable row that copies the ID to clipboard when clicked, with visual feedback showing a checkmark when copied.

states.name: Device Name Field
states.description: The Device Name field shows the human-readable name of the device. Like the Device ID, it is clickable for copy-to-clipboard functionality.

states.name: Platform Field
states.description: The Platform field shows the operating system/platform name with text-capitalize CSS, so values like 'windows' display as 'Windows'. It also supports copy-to-clipboard.

states.name: Device Info Loading State
states.description: While device info is being fetched from the backend, a loading indicator with a spinning refresh icon and 'Loading device info...' text is shown in place of the device fields.

states.name: Device Info Unavailable State
states.description: When device info fails to load (deviceInfo is null after loading completes), an italic message 'Unable to load device information.' is shown instead of the device fields.
states.precondition: Device info API call has failed or returned null

states.name: Device ID Tip Note
states.description: Below the device fields, a tip note encourages users to include their Device ID when reporting issues.

states.name: Tauri IPC Integration
states.description: The Debug page integrates with the Rust backend through three Tauri IPC commands: 'get_debug_settings' (load on mount), 'set_debug_settings' (save button), and 'get_device_info' (load on mount + refresh). These are the data sources for all displayed information.

states.name: Overall Page Layout
states.description: The Debug page is rendered inside the Settings container which provides a full-height flex layout with padding and scrollable content. The page itself uses a space-y-6 vertical layout with the section header at top, then the debug settings card, then the device information card.

description: Debug & Diagnostics page (Settings > Advanced) -- provides developer tools for troubleshooting GUI automation. The page contains two main sections: Debug Settings for configuring image match debug mode and top match candidate count, and Device Information for viewing and copying system identifiers (Device ID, Device Name, Platform). The page loads settings from the Rust backend via Tauri IPC commands and persists changes on explicit save. Device info supports copy-to-clipboard with visual feedback.
